# Reticle

> A non-invasive AI layer between you and your machine. Name a control or a piece of
> content; Reticle finds it and marks it where it lives — on any app, any surface.
> It runs on-device on macOS, reads only the pixels you see, and answers only in its
> own overlay. Nothing leaves your machine.

Reticle is a grounding engine and Swift SDK for macOS by Niv Dvir. It perceives the
screen the way a person does, from rendered pixels, so it works on surfaces where
tools that read the code underneath come up empty: native controls, canvas-drawn UIs,
and remote/VDI desktops.

## The site

- [Reticle](https://getreticle.com/): what it is, what it reaches that others can't, and a live demo.
- [Demo video](https://getreticle.com/reticle_demo_yc_2026-07.mp4): on-device grounding across a live web page and a native app.

## Engineering write-ups

- [On-Device Document Grounding on macOS: Getting Qwen2.5-VL to Actually Work in Swift](https://dev.to/nivdvir/building-a-real-time-screen-reader-on-macos-that-actually-works-471): the ten fixes that made Qwen2.5-VL grounding reliable in Swift.
- [Your parity gate must enforce the number you publish](https://dev.to/nivdvir/your-parity-gate-must-enforce-the-number-you-publish-a-testing-methodology-for-porting-ml-models-j4g): a testing methodology for porting ML models across runtimes.
- [max_pixels is a token budget in disguise](https://dev.to/nivdvir/maxpixels-is-a-token-budget-in-disguise-and-the-right-cap-depends-on-the-size-of-what-youre-l0c): why the right resolution cap depends on the size of what you're looking for.

## Upstream work

The Qwen2.5-VL fixes that make on-device grounding reliable in Swift were written by
Niv Dvir and merged into Apple's mlx-swift-lm: pull requests 238, 239, 242, 243 and 419
at https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift-lm
